mainTopic: Honoring the wealthy, the landlord's hold through stored items, a resident away for שבת, and the partition in a shared cistern
overview: This amud opens at the end of a story. רבי gives honor to visitors according to their wealth. רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי protests that בן בוניס, whose father owns a thousand ships and a thousand towns, is the richer one. The גמרא explains that רבי and רבי עקיבא honored the wealthy, based on רבא בר מרי's reading of a פסוק in תהלים. Back in הלכה, a landlord who stores a מוקצה item, like a plough pin, in his tenant's space keeps a real hold there, so the tenant does not forbid the courtyard. A new משנה asks whether someone who leaves home for שבת still forbids the courtyard: רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון give four views. רב rules like רבי שמעון, but only when the man went to his daughter's house, not his son's. A second משנה deals with a cistern shared by two courtyards, which needs a ten-טפחים partition. The גמרא then debates what 'below' and 'above' mean, and a new challenge from a beam in a ruin begins that finishes on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי calls for honor for a very wealthy visitor
steps.stepSummary: Continuing the story, רבי tells those present to make room for someone worth two hundred מנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Make room for one who owns two hundred מנה!
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of a story. בן בוניס has already come before רבי, and רבי called him a 'בן מאה מנה'. Now a different visitor arrives, and רבי tells his students to make even more room for this man, because he is worth two hundred מנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, רבי had told them to make room for בן בוניס, calling him worth one hundred מנה. Now a second man, who seems richer, arrives, and רבי gives him more honor. The point is that רבי's honor grows with the person's wealth, and this is what makes רבי ישמעאל speak up for בן בוניס in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Make room (clear a place) as a sign of honor
A large unit of money (100 זוז)
A person worth two hundred מנה, meaning someone very wealthy

steps.confusionAlert: This story is a side trip (אגדתא). It is not the main הלכה of the סוגיא. The גמרא comes back to the הלכות of עירובין in step 5.

phrases.english: Make room
phrases.notes: רבי is speaking to those sitting before him.

phrases.english: for one worth two hundred maneh.
phrases.notes: This goes one level higher than the earlier 'one hundred מנה'.

steps.triggerLanguage: פַּנּוּ מָקוֹם לְבֶן מָאתַיִם מָנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of בן בוניס that began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי gave public honor to a person according to his wealth.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל describes the father's enormous wealth
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי tells רבי that this boy's father owns a thousand ships and a thousand towns.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוסי said before him: רבי, this boy's father has a thousand ships at sea, and matching them, a thousand towns on land.
steps.whatsHappening: A student objects on behalf of בן בוניס. He tells רבי that בן בוניס's father ('אביו של זה') is far richer than the second visitor, so בן בוניס deserves even more honor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that the family is extremely wealthy, with property both at sea and on land. This sets up רבי's reply in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא, the son of רבי יוסי, who was present before רבי

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לְפָנָיו רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei said before him:
Rebbe, the father of this one
phrases.notes: He means בוניס, the boy's father.

phrases.english: has a thousand ships at sea,
and matching them, a thousand towns on land.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְפָנָיו רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds facts about the visitor's wealth that go beyond what רבי had stated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The visitor's father is enormously wealthy.

steps.title: רבי says the boy should dress to match his wealth
steps.stepSummary: רבי tells רבי ישמעאל to tell the father not to send his son to him in such plain clothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: When you reach his father, tell him: Do not send him before me in these clothes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי answers. If the family is that rich, the boy should come dressed in a way that shows it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Clothing that matches a person's status lets people give him the right honor. רבי is not turning the boy away. He wants the boy's clothes to reflect his standing so that he can be honored properly.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it means garments or clothing

steps.confusionAlert: Here כֵּלִים means clothes, not utensils or vessels.

phrases.english: He said to him: When you reach his father,
tell him: Do not send him
in these garments before me.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ לִכְשֶׁתַּגִּיעַ אֵצֶל אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי responds to the new information about the father's wealth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wealthy person should dress according to his status so that he is honored properly.

steps.title: Why רבי and רבי עקיבא honored the wealthy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי and רבי עקיבא honored the rich, based on רבא בר מרי's reading of a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי honored the wealthy, and רבי עקיבא honored the wealthy. This follows רבא בר מרי's teaching on the verse 'May he sit before God forever; mercy and truth, appoint that they preserve him.' When may a person sit before God forever? When he provides 'מן' (food portions) of kindness and truth to preserve others.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps back to give the reason behind the story. Honoring rich people is proper, and it has a basis in a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא בר מרי reads the word מַן as 'portions' of food, the way the מן fed בני ישראל. Wealthy people can feed and support others, and that kindness keeps the world going. So they deserve honor, a seat 'before God'.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא known for drawing teachings from פסוקים
Here read as 'portions' of food (related to the מן), meaning providing sustenance

steps.whatToRemember: Honoring the wealthy is not just flattery. It honors their ability to support and feed others, as רבא בר מרי reads in תהלים.

phrases.english: Rebbe would honor the wealthy.
Rabbi Akiva would honor the wealthy.
As Rava bar Mari expounded:
'May he sit forever before God;
phrases.notes: This פסוק is from תהלים סא:ח.

phrases.english: mercy and truth, appoint that they preserve him.'
When does one sit forever before God?
When he provides portions of kindness and truth that preserve him.
phrases.notes: Here מַן is understood as portions of food he gives to others.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מְכַבֵּד עֲשִׁירִים רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מְכַבֵּד עֲשִׁירִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the behavior shown in the story and gives it a source in a פסוק.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: It is proper to honor the wealthy because they sustain others, based on the reading of 'מַן יִנְצְרֻהוּ'.

steps.title: A plough pin is the example of the landlord's real hold
steps.stepSummary: Returning to הלכה, רבה בר בר חנה gives an example of storage that counts as the landlord's usage in the tenant's space: a plough pin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said: For example, a plough pin.
steps.whatsHappening: The side story is over, and the גמרא goes back to the עירובין discussion. רבה בר בר חנה gives a case where the landlord's stored item gives him a real hold (תפיסת יד) in the tenant's space.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plough pin is מוקצה, so the tenant cannot move it on שבת. The spot where it sits is therefore fixed as the landlord's. That is why the tenant's place counts as part of the landlord's home, and the tenant does not forbid the courtyard.

keyTerms.meaning: A plough pin, a work tool that is מוקצה on שבת
A real hold or fixed right of usage in a space

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this line as part of the story. It answers the earlier הלכה question about what counts as the landlord's usage in the tenant's quarters.

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said:
For example, a plough pin.
phrases.notes: It is מוקצה, so the tenant cannot remove it on שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר כְּגוֹן יָתֵד שֶׁל מַחֲרֵישָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side story and returns to the הלכה discussion that came before it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Storing a מוקצה item, such as a plough pin, in the tenant's space gives the landlord a fixed hold there.

steps.title: A ברייתא draws the line at whether the item may be moved
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן cites a ברייתא from דבי שמואל. A movable item does not give the landlord a hold, so the tenant forbids the courtyard. A non-movable item does give a hold, so the tenant does not forbid it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: The school of שמואל taught: An item that may be moved on שבת, the tenant forbids. An item that may not be moved on שבת, the tenant does not forbid.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן brings a ברייתא that states the general rule behind רבה בר בר חנה's example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the stored item may be moved on שבת, the tenant could just move it aside. Then the landlord has no real hold, the tenant counts as a separate resident, and he forbids the courtyard without an עירוב. If the item is מוקצה, it stays in place, the landlord has a real hold, and the tenant does not forbid.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא taught in the study hall of שמואל
May be moved on שבת (not מוקצה)
Forbids, meaning it makes carrying in the courtyard forbidden without an עירוב

steps.confusionAlert: 'אוסר' here describes the tenant's residence. With a movable item, the tenant still counts as a separate resident who forbids. It does not mean the item itself is forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the practical test for תפיסת יד in עירובין. The question is whether the landlord's stored item may be moved on שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: Movable item: the tenant forbids. מוקצה item: the landlord has a real hold, and the tenant does not forbid.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן, תָּנָא דְּבֵי שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: The school of Shmuel taught:
An item that may be moved on Shabbat, the tenant forbids.
An item that may not be moved on Shabbat,
the tenant does not forbid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן תָּנָא דְּבֵי שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the general rule that רבה בר בר חנה's plough-pin example illustrates.
steps.raayaObject: The principle that only a non-movable (מוקצה) stored item gives the landlord a real hold
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of דבי שמואל, cited by רב נחמן

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the rule about non-movable items
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if the tenant has the landlord's טבל, metal lumps, or anything else that may not be moved on שבת, the tenant does not forbid the courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: if he has טבל, or lumps of metal, or anything that may not be moved on שבת, he does not forbid the courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as the דבי שמואל source from step 6. It confirms that non-movable items give the landlord a hold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6, רב נחמן showed that only items that cannot be moved on שבת count as the landlord's real hold on the tenant's space. This ברייתא gives concrete examples: טבל and עששית. Because these items stay put all שבת, the landlord's 'presence' stays too, so the tenant counts as part of the landlord's household and does not forbid.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was also taught this way.' This phrase introduces a ברייתא that supports what was just said.
Produce that has not been tithed yet. It may not be moved on שבת.
A lump of glass or metal, which is not useful on שבת and so may not be moved.
Allowed to be moved on שבת.
Forbids. It means he makes carrying in the shared courtyard forbidden for the other residents.

steps.confusionAlert: 'אינו אוסר' does not mean the item is permitted to move. It means the tenant does not restrict the other residents from carrying in the courtyard, because he counts as part of the landlord's household.
steps.whatToRemember: Only items that cannot be moved on שבת (like טבל or עששית) give the landlord a real hold in the tenant's space. Then the tenant does not forbid the courtyard.

phrases.english: It was also taught so (in a ברייתא):
if he has untithed produce (of the landlord),
if he has lumps of glass or metal,
or anything that may not be moved on Shabbat —
he does not forbid (the courtyard).

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 6 with a second תנאי source that reaches the same ruling.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that only items not movable on שבת give the landlord a hold, so the tenant does not forbid.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing טבל, עששית, and any item not movable on שבת.

steps.title: New משנה: leaving home for שבת, and רבי מאיר says he still forbids
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens a new case. A resident leaves his house in a shared courtyard to spend שבת in another town. רבי מאיר says that whether he is a נכרי or a Jew, he still forbids the courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who leaves his house and goes to spend שבת in another town, whether a נכרי or a Jew, still forbids the courtyard. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It asks whether a resident who is away for שבת still restricts carrying in the shared courtyard, and it starts with רבי מאיר's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually every resident of a courtyard must join the עירוב, or else carrying is forbidden. רבי מאיר holds that a house still counts as a residence even when its owner is far away. So the absent resident still forbids the courtyard, just as if he were home.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. It marks the start of a new משנה.
One who leaves his house behind.
'The words of רבי מאיר.' This attributes the view just stated.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who leaves his house
and goes to spend Shabbat in another town,
whether a gentile or a Jew —
he forbids (the courtyard),
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמַּנִּיחַ בֵּיתוֹ וְהָלַךְ לִשְׁבּוֹת בְּעִיר אַחֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. The topic shifts from the landlord's items to a resident who is away from home.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: an absent resident, whether a נכרי or a Jew, still forbids the courtyard.

steps.title: רבי יהודה says the absent resident does not forbid
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees with רבי מאיר and holds that the absent resident does not forbid the courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: He does not forbid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the opposing view to רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, a house with nobody living in it over שבת is just an empty residence. It does not count as a resident who needs to join the עירוב. So both a נכרי and a Jew who are away do not forbid the courtyard.

keyTerms.meaning: Says. This word introduces a תנא's opinion.
A residence. The question is whether an empty one still counts.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: He does not forbid.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ אוֹסֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly disputes רבי מאיר in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: an absent resident does not forbid the courtyard.

steps.title: רבי יוסי splits it: a נכרי forbids, a Jew does not
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי takes a middle view. An absent נכרי forbids, but an absent Jew does not, because a Jew does not usually come home on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: A נכרי forbids, but a Jew does not forbid, because it is not the way of a Jew to come home on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion in the משנה splits between a נכרי and a Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key question for רבי יוסי is whether the person might come back during שבת. A Jew will not travel home on שבת, so he has truly left, and his house does not forbid. A נכרי might return at any time, so he has not really left, and he still forbids.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבי יוסי makes the rule depend on whether the person is realistically likely to return. רבי שמעון builds on that idea in the next step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
a gentile forbids,
a Jew does not forbid,
because it is not the way of a Jew to come (home) on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: נׇכְרִי — אוֹסֵר, יִשְׂרָאֵל — אֵינוֹ אוֹסֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes a middle position between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: an absent נכרי forbids, and an absent Jew does not, since a Jew will not return on שבת.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: even in the same town, a Jew who left does not forbid
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון goes further. Even if the Jew only went to his daughter's house in the same town, he does not forbid, because he has already put his home out of his mind for שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: Even if he left his house and went to spend שבת with his daughter in the same town, he does not forbid, because he has already removed it from his mind.
steps.whatsHappening: The final opinion in the משנה makes the Jew's case even more lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's reason was that the Jew cannot travel back on שבת. But in the same town he easily could walk back. רבי שמעון says it still does not matter: once he decided to spend שבת elsewhere, he mentally left his house (הסיע מלבו), so it does not forbid.

keyTerms.meaning: Even. It signals a bigger case than the one before.
He removed it from his mind. He has decided not to return home.

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון's reason is not distance. In the same town the man could easily walk home. The reason is his decision: he has made his שבת place somewhere else.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has four views. רבי מאיר: he always forbids. רבי יהודה: he never forbids. רבי יוסי: a נכרי forbids and a Jew does not. רבי שמעון: a Jew does not forbid, even in the same town, because he put his home out of mind.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Even if he left his house
and went to spend Shabbat with his daughter
in the same town —
he does not forbid,
because he has already removed (returning home) from his mind.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ הִנִּיחַ בֵּיתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds past רבי יוסי. Even a Jew who could easily return does not forbid, because the test is his intention.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון: a Jew who leaves to spend שבת elsewhere, even in the same town, does not forbid, since he has already removed his home from his mind.

steps.title: רב rules like רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון: a Jew who goes to his daughter's house in the same town does not forbid the courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב said: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by giving the final ruling on the משנה's argument. רב says we follow רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון held that a Jew who went away for שבת does not forbid the courtyard, even if he only went to his daughter's house in the same town, because he has put his home out of his mind. רב makes that the practical הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the practical answer to the four-way argument in steps 8-11.

phrases.english: Gemara:
Rav said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the dispute laid out in the משנה.

steps.title: Only a daughter's house, not a son's
steps.stepSummary: The ruling like רבי שמעון applies only when the man went to his daughter's house. If he went to his son's house, he still forbids the courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is only for his daughter's house, but his son's house, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows רב's ruling. The leniency only works if he went to his daughter's house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At his son's house, he might not feel settled and could come back home on שבת. So we cannot assume he has put his home out of his mind, and he still forbids the courtyard.

phrases.english: And this is only his daughter's house,
but his son's house — no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדַוְקָא בִּתּוֹ, אֲבָל בְּנוֹ — לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ruling of step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only going to a daughter's house counts; a son's house does not.

steps.title: A folk saying about the dog
steps.stepSummary: A popular saying backs up the difference: a male dog's bark can be ignored, but a female dog's bark means you should leave.
steps.simpleTranslation: As people say: If a male dog barks at you, go in; if a female dog barks at you, go out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports the daughter/son difference with a saying people used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At a daughter's house, the son-in-law is the 'male dog': his complaints are easy to live with, so the father stays. At a son's house, the daughter-in-law is the 'female dog': if she objects, the son will not stand against her, so the father may end up going home on שבת.
steps.confusionAlert: The saying is not about real dogs. The male dog stands for the son-in-law and the female dog for the daughter-in-law.

phrases.english: As people say:
If a male dog barks at you — enter,
if a female dog barks at you — leave.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the limit in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: The difference between a daughter's house and a son's house.
steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון, but only for a daughter's house. At a son's house the daughter-in-law may push him out, so he could return home.

steps.title: A cistern between two courtyards
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: no one may draw water on שבת from a cistern shared by two courtyards unless a partition ten טפחים high divides it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A cistern between two courtyards: one may not draw from it on שבת unless a partition ten טפחים high was made for it, whether below or within its rim.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts a new topic. It is about a cistern that sits partly in each of two courtyards.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a divider, someone in one courtyard might draw water from the other courtyard's area. A partition ten טפחים high separates the two areas. It works whether it is placed low, near the water, or higher up inside the cistern below its rim.

keyTerms.meaning: Ten handbreadths, the minimum height for a halachic partition

phrases.english: Mishnah:
A cistern that is between two courtyards —
one may not draw water from it on Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן עָשׂוּ לוֹ מְחִיצָה
phrases.english: unless they made a partition for it
ten handbreadths high,
whether below, or within its rim.

steps.triggerLanguage: בּוֹר שֶׁבֵּין שְׁתֵּי חֲצֵירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה with a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A shared cistern needs a ten-טפחים partition, placed either below or within the rim, before anyone may draw from it on שבת.

steps.title: בית שמאי and בית הלל on where the partition goes
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל reports an older dispute: בית שמאי say the partition must be below, and בית הלל say above.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: בית שמאי say below, and בית הלל say above.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל tells us that the placement of the partition was argued over long ago.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the משנה allowed either placement. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל shows that the question was really disputed by בית שמאי and בית הלל. The גמרא explains what exactly 'below' and 'above' mean in steps 18-19.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Beit Shammai say: below,
and Beit Hillel say: above.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a disagreement about where the partition from step 15 should be placed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: the partition goes below. בית הלל: the partition goes above.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the wall above is enough
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says no extra partition is needed, because the wall between the two courtyards already passes over the cistern.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: A partition should not be better than the wall between them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives the most lenient view: you do not need a new partition inside the cistern at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The courtyard wall already runs across the top of the cistern. In his view, a small partition inside the cistern would do no more than that wall, so the wall is enough to divide it.

keyTerms.meaning: Should not be better or stronger than

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
A partition should not be greater
than the wall between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: לֹא תְּהֵא מְחִיצָה גְּדוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the need for a partition at all.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wall between the courtyards is enough; no extra partition is needed.

steps.title: רב הונא explains 'below' and 'above'
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says 'below' means low in the cistern and 'above' means high in the cistern. Both are inside the cistern's open space.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב הונא said: Below means truly below, above means truly above, and both are within the cistern.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the words 'below' and 'above' from the dispute of בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב הונא, both opinions place the partition inside the cistern's open space. בית שמאי want it low, near the water, and בית הלל want it high, near the rim. According to רב הונא's view, neither one requires the partition to go into the water.

phrases.english: Gemara:
Rav Huna said:
Below — truly below,
above — truly above,
and both of these are within the cistern.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: לְמַטָּה — לְמַטָּה מַמָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the terms used in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Below' is low in the cistern and 'above' is high in the cistern; both are inside the cistern's open space.

steps.title: רב יהודה: measured from the water
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says 'below' means below the water, so the partition goes into the water. 'Above' means above the water.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said: Below means below the water; above means above the water.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives a different explanation of the same two words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב יהודה, the line between the two views is the surface of the water. בית שמאי require the partition to be placed down in the water. בית הלל allow it to be placed above the water. Steps 21 and 23 add that either way the partition must cross the waterline by a טפח.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, not the same person as the תנא רבי יהודה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רב יהודה, the אמורא in this step, with רבי יהודה, the תנא in the משנה who said the wall is enough.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said:
Below — below the water,
above — above the water.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר: לְמַטָּה — לְמַטָּה מִן הַמַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different explanation from רב הונא's in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Below' means in the water; 'above' means above the water.
steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא explains both opinions as places inside the cistern's open space. רב יהודה uses the water's surface as the dividing line, so בית שמאי require the partition to go into the water.

steps.title: Won't the water mix even with a partition below the water?
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב חנן challenges רב יהודה. If a partition low in the empty space of the cistern fails because the water mixes, a partition under the water should fail too, since the water above it mixes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב חנן said to אביי: About what רב יהודה said, that 'below' means below the water: why does a partition that is truly 'below' (low in the empty space, near the water) not work? Because the water mixes underneath it. But a partition below the water has the same problem. The water mixes above it!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב חנן asks אביי a question that attacks the logic of רב יהודה's explanation from Step 19.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה rejected רב הונא's view that 'below' means low in the open space of the cistern. The reason was that the water could still flow freely under that partition. רבה בר רב חנן points out that a partition sunk inside the water seems to have the same flaw, because the water above its top flows freely between the two sides.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference? (asks why two cases are treated differently)
Truly 'below,' meaning low in the open air of the cistern
Below (under the surface of) the water

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'below' (לְמַטָּה מַמָּשׁ) means low in the air space of the cistern, the way רב הונא explained it. It does not mean underwater. רב יהודה's 'below the water' is the underwater version.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּה בַּר רַב חָנָן לְאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Ḥanan said to Abaye:
That which Rav Yehuda said,
"Below" means below the water:
phrases.notes: This is quoting what we saw back in Step 19.

phrases.english: Why does a partition actually below (in the open space) not work?
Because the water mixes together.

phrases.aramaic: לְמַטָּה מִן הַמַּיִם נָמֵי, הָא עֲרִיבִי מַיָּא?!
phrases.english: Below the water as well, the water mixes (above it)!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא לְמַטָּה מַמָּשׁ דְּלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יהודה's explanation from Step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's reading that 'below' means below the water
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason that disqualifies a partition in the open space (the water mixes) seems to apply just as much to a partition sunk under the water.

steps.title: The reeds must stick out a טפח above the water
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the reeds of an underwater partition must rise a טפח above the surface, so no water passes over the top.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Didn't you hear what רב יהודה said in the name of רב, and some attribute it to רבי חייא? The tops of the reeds must be visible a טפח above the water.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question by citing an earlier teaching about how the underwater partition must be built.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'below the water' partition does not stay fully underwater. It starts down in the water and rises at least a טפח above the surface. So the water is completely divided, and the mixing problem disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: Didn't you hear? (introduces a known source as the answer)
And some trace it back to (an alternate attribution)

phrases.english: He said to him: Did you not hear

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב,
phrases.english: that which Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav,
and some attribute it to Rabbi Ḥiyya:
The tops of the reeds must be visible
a handbreadth above the water.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ הָא דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying how the partition is built, based on an earlier source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An underwater partition lies fully under the surface, so water mixes above it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The underwater partition rises a טפח above the surface, so the water is fully divided.

steps.title: Won't the water mix even with a partition above the water?
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב חנן asks the parallel question. If a partition at the cistern's rim fails because the water mixes beneath it, a partition just above the water should fail for the same reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: And further: About what רב יהודה said, that 'above' means above the water: why does a partition that is truly 'above' (up near the rim) not work? Because the water mixes underneath it. But a partition above the water has the same problem. The water mixes under it!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב חנן asks a second question that mirrors the first one, this time about the 'above' position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A partition hanging over the water seems no better than one up at the rim. Either way, the water below it flows freely between the two sides.

keyTerms.meaning: Truly 'above,' meaning up near the rim of the cistern
Above the surface of the water

phrases.english: And further, that which Rav Yehuda said:
"Above" means above the water.
Why does a partition actually above (at the rim) not work?
Because the water mixes together.

phrases.aramaic: לְמַעְלָה מִן הַמַּיִם נָמֵי, הָא עֲרִיבִי מַיָּא?!
phrases.english: Above the water as well, the water mixes (beneath it)!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ, הָא דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel second question, same structure as Step 20
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's reading that 'above' means above the water
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The water flows freely under a partition above the water, just as it does under one at the rim.

steps.title: The reeds must dip a טפח into the water
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers with יעקב קרחינאה's teaching that the reed ends must be sunk a טפח into the water.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Didn't you hear what יעקב קרחינאה taught? One must sink the ends of the reeds a טפח into the water.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the second question with another earlier teaching about how the partition is built.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'above the water' partition hangs down from above, but its lower edge must dip at least a טפח into the water. This divides the water at the surface. Together with Step 21, the result is that both positions in רב יהודה's view cross the waterline by a טפח.

keyTerms.meaning: יעקב from Karḥina, a teacher of ברייתות
That he should sink or immerse

steps.whatToRemember: In רב יהודה's view, a partition 'below the water' must stick out a טפח above the surface. A partition 'above the water' must dip a טפח into it. Either way, the partition crosses the waterline.

phrases.english: He said to him: Did you not hear
that which Ya'akov of Karḥina taught:
One must sink the ends of the reeds
a handbreadth into the water.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ הָא דְּתָנֵי יַעֲקֹב קַרְחִינָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying how the partition is built, based on an earlier source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A partition above the water does not touch it, so water mixes beneath it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The partition's lower edge dips a טפח into the water, so the water is divided.

steps.title: Opening a third challenge from the beam in a ruin
steps.stepSummary: The questioning goes on with a further challenge (the text names no speaker here). He cites רב יהודה's ruling that a beam four טפחים wide permits carrying in a ruin, and then introduces רב נחמן's report in the name of רבה בר אבוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, what about what רב יהודה said: a beam of four טפחים permits carrying in a ruin. And רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge by quoting another ruling of רב יהודה. The actual question finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A beam four טפחים wide laid across a ruin is viewed as if its edges extend down to the ground, forming partitions. This idea of a 'virtual' partition seems to clash with what was just said, that a cistern partition must physically reach into or above the water. רב נחמן's quote in the name of רבה בר אבוה begins here, and its content will complete the challenge.
steps.confusionAlert: This step stops in the middle of a sentence. רבה בר אבוה's statement and the actual question continue on the next amud.

phrases.english: But then, that which Rav Yehuda said:
A beam of four handbreadths permits carrying in a ruin,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: and Rav Naḥman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
phrases.notes: The statement continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא הָא דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After two questions are answered, a third challenge is opened from a different ruling of רב יהודה
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's requirement that the cistern partition physically cross the water
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only. It contrasts a cistern partition that must physically reach the water with a beam whose edges are viewed as reaching the ground (completed on the next amud).
